Job Description

***This position is open to remote candidates within the United States. Candidates located in the Atlanta, Indianapolis, or Charlotte/Cherryville markets will be expected to work from a local Cox office 2-3 days per week to support in-person collaboration.

The Senior Manager, Change Enablement is responsible for leading and executing change enablement strategies that support strategic initiatives across the Fleet business. This role plays a critical part in driving adoption of business process, system, and organizational changes by ensuring employees are prepared, supported, and engaged throughout the change journey.

Working closely with business leaders, project teams, and functional partners, the Senior Manager develops and executes change strategies that align with business objectives and enable successful adoption of new ways of working. This role partners closely with Learning & Development teams to identify learning needs, define learning strategies, and coordinate execution plans that support change readiness and adoption; however, the role does not design, develop, or manage learning programs.

The ideal candidate brings strong consulting, stakeholder management, communication, and analytical skills, with the ability to influence across a matrixed organization and translate business objectives into practical change plans that drive measurable outcomes.

PRIMARY DUTIES/KEY RESPONSIBILITES

  • Lead change enablement activities for strategic initiatives, including change impact assessments, stakeholder engagement, communications, readiness planning, and adoption measurement.

  • Develop and execute comprehensive change strategies that support successful implementation of business, process, and technology changes.

  • Partner with business leaders, project teams, and subject matter experts to assess organizational impacts and adoption risks.

  • Collaborate with Learning & Development partners to identify capability gaps, align learning strategies to business needs, and coordinate learning execution plans that support change adoption.

  • Advise initiative leaders on change enablement best practices and effective approaches to stakeholder engagement and adoption.

  • Build and maintain strong relationships with stakeholders across multiple functions and organizational levels.

  • Facilitate workshops, planning sessions, and stakeholder discussions to support alignment and successful change outcomes.

  • Support leadership sponsorship activities by equipping leaders with the tools, messaging, and resources needed to lead change effectively.

  • Monitor change readiness, adoption metrics, and business outcomes, providing recommendations to improve effectiveness and mitigate risks.

  • Analyze data and stakeholder feedback to identify trends, opportunities, and potential barriers to adoption.

  • Drive cross-functional alignment and help resolve competing priorities that may impact initiative success.

  • Provide regular updates regarding change progress, adoption performance, risks, and mitigation plans.

  • Contribute to the continuous improvement of change enablement/change readiness methodologies, tools, templates, and frameworks.

  • Lead special projects and strategic initiatives as assigned.

Required Experience & Specialized Knowledge

  • Bachelor's degree in a related field (such as Change Management, Organizational Effectiveness, Program Management, Consulting, or a similar discipline) with 8+ years of experience leading change management initiatives within business transformation and/or business process redesign environments. Equivalent combinations of education and experience will be considered, including a master's degree with 6+ years of relevant experience, a Ph.D. with 3+ years of relevant experience, or 12+ years of related professional experience.

  • Change Management, Organizational Effectiveness, Program Management, Consulting, or related fields.

  • Proven experience leading change initiatives supporting technology, process, and organizational transformation.

  • Strong knowledge of change management methodologies and adoption practices.

  • Demonstrated ability to influence and drive outcomes in a highly matrixed environment without direct authority.

  • Excellent communication, facilitation, stakeholder management, and presentation skills.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities.

  • Experience partnering with senior leaders and cross-functional teams to achieve business objectives.

  • Up to 25% travel may be required.

Drug Testing

To be employed in this role, you’ll need to clear a pre-employment drug test. Cox Automotive does not currently administer a pre-employment drug test for marijuana for this position. However, we are a drug-free workplace, so the possession, use or being under the influence of drugs illegal under federal or state law during work hours, on company property and/or in company vehicles is prohibited.

Benefits

The Company offers eligible employees the flexibility to take as much vacation with pay as they deem consistent with their duties, the company’s needs, and its obligations; seven paid holidays throughout the calendar year; and up to 160 hours of paid wellness annually for their own wellness or that of family members. Employees are also eligible for additional paid time off in the form of bereavement leave, time off to vote, jury duty leave, volunteer time off, military leave, and parental leave.

About Us

Through groundbreaking technology and a commitment to stellar experiences for drivers and dealers alike, Cox Automotive employees are transforming the way the world buys, owns, sells – or simply uses – cars. Cox Automotive employees get to work on iconic consumer brands like Autotrader and Kelley Blue Book and industry-leading dealer-facing companies like vAuto and Manheim, all while enjoying the people-centered atmosphere that is central to our life at Cox. Benefits of working at Cox may include health care insurance (medical, dental, vision), retirement planning (401(k)), and paid days off (sick leave, parental leave, flexible vacation/wellness days, and/or PTO). For more details on what benefits you may be offered, visit our benefits page. Cox is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer – All qualified applicants/employees will receive consideration for employment without regard to that individual’s age, race, color, religion or creed, national origin or ancestry, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, physical or mental disability, veteran status, genetic information, ethnicity, citizenship, or any other characteristic protected by law. Cox provides reasonable accommodations when requested by a qualified applicant or employee with disability, unless such accommodations would cause an undue hardship.

EOE, including disability/vets

 

 

Applicants must currently be authorized to work in the United States for any employer without current or future sponsorship. No OPT, CPT, STEM/OPT or visa sponsorship now or in future.


 


 

Application Deadline: 08/09/2026

Centene is transforming the health of our communities one person at a time. As an Executive on our team, you could be the one who changes everything for our 28 million members.
 

Position Purpose: Leads the enterprise change communications function, providing strategic direction, governance, and executive communications support for the organization's largest transformation initiatives, including enterprise modernization, organizational change, mergers and acquisitions, and business integration efforts.

  • Develops the enterprise change communications strategy aligned to business priorities.
  • Serves as the senior communications advisor to executive leadership and the Transformation Office.
  • Leads communications for enterprise transformation initiatives and organizational change programs.
  • Oversees executive messaging, leadership communications, and enterprise change campaigns.
  • Establishes governance, standards, and best practices for change communications.
  • Partners with HR, Transformation Office, and other key stakeholders and business leaders to drive alignment on how we plan and respond to change.
  • Develops measurement frameworks to evaluate communication effectiveness and adoption.
  • Leads, coaches, and develops a high-performing team of change communications professionals.
  • Manages multiple enterprise initiatives while ensuring consistent messaging.
  • Identifies communication risks and develop mitigation strategies.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.
  • Complies with all policies and standards.

Education/Experience: Bachelor's Degree Communications or related field required.
10+ years leadership experience, with progressive responsibility in corporate communications.
Demonstrated experience to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
Experience in a highly regulated environment.
Or equivalent experience acquired through accomplishments of applicable knowledge, duties, scope and skill reflective of the level of this position.

Pay Range: $188,900.00 - $359,800.00 per year

Total compensation may also include additional forms of incentives. Benefits may be subject to program eligibility.

Position Purpose: Develops, assesses, and facilitates complex care management activities for primarily mental and behavioral health needs members to provide high quality, cost-effective healthcare outcomes including personalized care plans and education for members and their families related to mental health and substance use disorder.

Position Purpose: Analyzes all prior authorization requests to determine medical necessity of service and appropriate level of care in accordance with national standards, contractual requirements, and a member's benefit coverage.   • Provides feedback on opportunities to improve the authorization review process for members
  • Performs other duties as assigned

Clinical knowledge and ability to analyze authorization requests and determine medical necessity of service preferred.
Knowledge of Medicare and Medicaid regulations preferred.

Hospice experience preferred.
